hook_text: Fifty-three kidnapped Africans. One nail. A ship called Friendship.
clip_script: 1839. Men, women and children from Sierra Leone are kidnapped and shipped illegally to Cuba. Put aboard a schooner called La Amistad, which means friendship, they find a way to break their chains. Led by a young rice farmer, Sengbe Pieh, they seize the ship and order the crew to sail home to Africa. But the Spanish sailors trick them, steering north by night. Two months later, the ship is captured off New York and the Africans are jailed. Spain demands them back as property. Abolitionists find an interpreter who speaks their language, and their story is finally heard. In 1841 the Supreme Court rules: they were kidnapped, and they are free. The next year, they sail home.
visual_style: A whiteboard schooner on a dark sea; a broken chain; a compass needle secretly turning north; a courtroom with a judge's gavel; a ship sailing east into a rising sun.
pacing: Three-beat hook, fast adventure, a courtroom climax and calm homecoming.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and meet the rebels who fought slavery.
